cells.why: On JetStream a retry is deduped only inside the stream's dedup window, and only until the row's next write (E-44, measured). A keyed call with its own ttl and a stored first result was not built on it.
cells.closes: a keyed call built on the outside log, then the retried-call chaos phase on real runs
cells.why2: A claim row per key works on JetStream as 'publish only if the subject is empty' (E-44's lock: 60 acquires through a leader kill, never two holders). But a re-run's writes are counted twice after the row's next write, and expiry is per stream, so one ttl per stream (E-44 gaps 2 and 7).

cells.why: E-22 built the tape as an L5 library on the L4 verbs (a resource with a time window, rows keyed by match key). Record, find by match key, replay in order and forget past the window passed in all 100 seeds of each mode, with a leader change and a slot move forced in. One tape is one partition, so it has one writer (D14); the 14 days ran on virtual time.
cells.why2: E-22's P-18 check records a tape as a resource, finds an answer by match key, replays in order and forgets past its window. It passed in 300 of 300 worlds in each of the three modes. A tape keeps its recordings in one partition, so replay order is that partition's log order (a simulation; no real disk).

cells.why: E-06 measured it through fero's real seam with data. At the cafe's size (1e3 rows) a rerun from a snapshot costs 0.6 to 1.2 ms, and undoing a rerun's own records costs 0.03 to 0.05 ms at every size (bar 10 ms). Undo serves reruns in tape order and needs one small data change to keep key order after a removed row (A-10); a jump costs the inputs between.
cells.why2: Undoing a rerun's records by their inverses costs 0.03 to 0.05 ms at every size up to 1e6 rows, and a rerun from a snapshot costs 0.6 to 1.2 ms at the café's size, against 10 ms (E-06, on fero v4's real seam with data). It serves reruns in tape order; a jump costs the inputs between. A group view adds its own cost (165 ms at 1e6 rows) until data's group emits per-row deltas (A-10).

cells.why: Step 1: v4 is leaderless LWW per cell (R `lww`), so two members can each take a conditional write on one row and both answer ok; DESIGN-V5 section 9 measured it (two sells of the last item, both ok). Step 2: a history with two such ok answers has no order that explains both. Step 3: so v4's per-partition histories of conditional writes cannot pass Porcupine as linearizable.
cells.why2: Step 1: TEST-13 asks that per-partition histories pass Porcupine as linearizable. Step 2: v4 merges cells by last-writer-wins and collects tombstones, and STATUS.md pins two red probes on today's kernel: a later remove loses to an older write after a heal, and one forwarded write commits twice across an ownership move. Step 3: in each, an acknowledged operation is undone or applied twice, and no linear order explains that. Step 4: the root is the row's R option: last-writer-wins cannot hold conditions without consensus (SPACE section 2 R, cited).

cells.why: Judge 1 is right; I confirm each step. Step 1: a CELL resource has a cell count fixed when it is defined, 16 by default (V5-PRIMITIVE; SPACE P `fixN`). Step 2: 16 cells give 7 to 15 writers' worth under skew (E-18, B4), below F_w = 64, so the resource must grow past 16 to reach the floor. Step 3: its only growth is a re-key into a new generation with more cells, and E-17 part 1 says "the count is chosen per re-key". Step 4: nothing in the row chooses it: its P cell has no `+ rule`, its C is `self` (healing only, no planner), and SPACE's ladder keeps the automatic grow rule as one more mechanism on the slot path, outside CELL's count of about 3. So a person picks a shard count to grow, at define time or at a re-key; a rule that picks it would be another row's option. That answers judge 2's open point (who picks). cells.why: Judge 2 is right; I confirm each step. Step 1: OPS-05 asks that a roll across two kernel builds works, with new behaviour held back by a cluster version until every member is new. Step 2: v4 has no cluster version, and its decision V4-14 says mixed versions are unsupported (STATUS.md). Step 3: its code makes a mixed pair refuse each other on purpose: the door's proof label was raised so that an old and a new member both fail `bad-proof` (kernel/door.ts; DECISIONS, V4-55), and an old feeder strands its clients' writes (DECISIONS, V4-43). Step 4: so in a roll across such builds the first restarted member is refused by the rest, and the roll test fails; the supported way is to stop every member (README, "Mixed versions do not link").

cells.why2: Its hosted shape pools projects in one log-tier process, where a tenant at its quota raised another's p99 by 1.40 to 1.59 times against SC-11's 1.1 (E-35). A-29 gives it a byte budget per tenant (about 1 MiB/s here) or a volume per tenant; neither is built, nor are keys per project or the cross-project read test.
